skill.name: deploy-model
skill.description: Guides Azure AI Foundry model deployment through preset, customized, and capacity discovery workflows. It checks Azure authentication, project scope, model availability, quota, SKU options, and deployment confirmation steps.
skill.summary: Deploy Azure AI Foundry models with capacity checks, configuration guidance, and confirmation steps.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: The static findings are largely false positives from Markdown code fences, relative documentation links, official Azure endpoints, and expected Azure CLI helper scripts. No prompt-injection attempt was found; the jailbreak keyword hit is an Azure Prompt Shield policy reference. A critical semantic issue remains in capacity/scripts/discover_and_rank.sh because it constructs inline Python from unescaped shell variables.

remediation.issue: Unsanitized inline Python in capacity discovery helper
remediation.suggestion: Replace python3 -c interpolation with a script or heredoc that reads JSON from stdin and arguments from sys.argv. Validate MIN_CAPACITY as an integer before use.
Validate model names, versions, regions, SKUs, and capacity values with strict allowlists before passing them to Azure CLI, jq, or Python.

remediation.issue: Predictable temporary file path in workflow examples
remediation.suggestion: Use mktemp or a scoped temporary directory for capacity JSON examples, then delete the file after processing.

semantic_findings.description: capacity/scripts/discover_and_rank.sh builds a python3 -c program with shell variables and JSON interpolated directly into Python source. A crafted model, version, or minimum capacity argument could break out of string literals and run local Python code when the helper script is executed.

content.value_statement: Azure model deployment often requires checking model availability, quota, region, and SKU options. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through capacity checks, confirmation, and deployment steps.
actual_capabilities: Routes requests between quick preset deployment, custom deployment, and capacity discovery workflows.
Checks Azure CLI authentication and confirms the target Azure AI Foundry project before deployment.
Queries live model availability, regional capacity, SKU support, and subscription quota.
Guides model version, SKU, capacity, RAI policy, and advanced option selection.
Creates and monitors Azure AI Foundry model deployments after user confirmation.
Generates Azure AI Foundry portal links for completed deployments.
limitations: Requires Azure CLI access and permissions in the target subscription.
Capacity, quota, and model availability depend on live Azure service data.
Deployment actions can create billable Azure resources.
Does not manage existing deployments except for status checks and troubleshooting guidance.

use_cases.title: Deploy a model quickly
use_cases.description: Choose a model and let the workflow find a suitable region and default deployment settings.

use_cases.title: Plan capacity across regions
use_cases.description: Compare Azure regions and projects before committing to a model deployment.

use_cases.title: Configure governed deployments
use_cases.description: Select model version, SKU, capacity, RAI policy, and upgrade behavior for controlled environments.

prompt_templates.title: Quick model deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Deploy gpt-4o-mini to my Azure AI Foundry project with recommended defaults. Confirm the target project before creating anything.

prompt_templates.title: Capacity discovery
prompt_templates.scenario: Find a viable region before deployment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find where I can deploy gpt-4o with at least 50K TPM. Show regions, quota, and matching projects before I choose.

prompt_templates.title: Custom deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Deploy gpt-4o with a chosen version, GlobalStandard SKU, custom capacity, and the Microsoft.DefaultV2 RAI policy.

prompt_templates.title: Production deployment planning
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with policy and quota constraints.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a production Azure AI Foundry deployment for a high-volume model. Compare SKU choices, quota limits, upgrade policy, and confirmation steps.

output_examples.output: The skill confirms the active subscription and project, checks model capacity, selects a suitable region, and asks for approval before deployment.

output_examples.input: Find a region with 100K TPM for gpt-4o.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a ranked region list with capacity, quota status, available projects, and recommended next actions.
The skill guides version, SKU, capacity, advanced options, review, deployment execution, and status monitoring.

best_practices: Confirm subscription, project, region, SKU, and capacity before creating resources.
Use live Azure quota and model catalog data instead of hardcoded availability lists.
Start with conservative capacity and monitor usage before increasing throughput.
anti_patterns: Deploying without showing the target project and subscription to the user.
Assuming a model or SKU is available without checking live Azure capacity.
Using custom RAI policies or PTU settings without validating organizational requirements.

faq.question: Does this skill require Azure CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflows assume Azure CLI is installed, authenticated, and authorized for the target subscription.

faq.question: Can it choose the best Azure region?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare regional capacity and quota, then recommend suitable deployment locations.

faq.question: Does it support custom deployment settings?
faq.answer: Yes. The custom workflow covers model version, SKU, capacity, RAI policy, upgrade policy, and advanced options.

faq.question: Will it create billable resources?
faq.answer: It can create Azure model deployments after user confirmation, which may incur Azure charges.

faq.question: Can it list or delete existing deployments?
faq.answer: No. It may show troubleshooting commands, but listing and deletion are outside the primary skill scope.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
